entries.what_happened: One manuscript, 'Nonhomeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds with the same homotopy type' (OpenAI, dated October 4, 2026). Theorem 'pair' (thm:pair): there are closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds M and N that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, with a common word-hyperbolic fundamental group Π. Theorem 'self-map' (thm:self-map): for the same M there is a homotopy equivalence f: M → M such that no homeomorphism M → M is homotopic to f. Construction in outline: a four-dimensional Poincaré chamber (D, P, S) whose double cyclic cover S₂ has a marked filling, while every odd cyclic cover S_d (d ≥ 3) has none. Reflection quotient Q of P by an elementary abelian label group A = (ℤ/2)^𝒱 / C, where 𝒱 is the vertex set of a flag-no-square triangulation of S with at least 5000 vertices and C is an explicit 8-dimensional subspace; Q₂ is the double cyclic cover of Q, and Π = π₁(Q₂). M = M₀ and N = M_ℓ are two closed manifold models of Q₂, obtained by gluing copies of a topological filling of S₂ with boundary twists given by a linear functional ε on A (ε = 0 for M, ε = ℓ ≠ 0 for N). Self-map: a cyclic-cover criterion realizes the outer automorphism δ of Π by a self-homotopy equivalence of M and rules out any homeomorphism inducing δ. Non-homeomorphism: a Sylow-type criterion for Out(Π) (Proposition 'A Sylow criterion for manifold models'), using that A and B_ℓ are 2-subgroups of equal order, that the normalizer of A in Out(Π) is A × ⟨δ⟩, that δ is not realized on M, and that A and B_ℓ are not conjugate in Out(Π).
entries.delivers: Dimension four only. The objects are closed connected aspherical topological (not smooth) four-manifolds. The pair M, N has one common fundamental group Π, which the text shows is word-hyperbolic, torsion-free, infinite, one-ended, and of finite index in the reflection extension W ⋊ H. Out(Π) is finite. The text claims a disproof of the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four, for this one group. Against the list's bullet, which asks for aspherical closed manifolds with isomorphic fundamental groups to be homeomorphic and does not restrict the dimension, the paper's existence form matches the bullet's wording, and the dimension-four pair falsifies that bullet as worded. The manuscripts do not claim to settle the Borel conjecture as a whole. Their statement is narrower than the bullet in dimension, and the bullet's part (3), the homotopy-realization form, is not the paper's headline. Reading the stated Theorem 'self-map' against the introduction's definition of the topological Borel conjecture (every homotopy equivalence between closed aspherical manifolds is homotopic to a homeomorphism), it also refutes that stronger form in dimension four. The text does not state that consequence in its abstract or introduction. It is my reading of the stated theorem. The text notes that Bartels and Lück prove the prescribed-class formulation in dimensions at least five for a class containing word-hyperbolic groups. The counterexample is in dimension four, so it does not conflict with that.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, the family does not touch these parts of the problem. (a) Dimensions other than four. The text treats dimensions at most two as classical, and dimension three for closed orientable aspherical manifolds via geometrization. It cites Bartels and Lück for dimensions at least five for a class containing hyperbolic groups. It says the cyclic-cover criterion 'works in every manifold dimension', but applies it only at n = 4. (b) Dimension four for other fundamental groups. The text does not characterize which dimension-four groups admit such pairs, and it gives only this one group. (c) The homotopy-realization form for other manifolds or groups. It is refuted only by the single self-map of M. (d) Goodness. The introduction presents goodness as the hypothesis of the dimension-four rigidity results it cites (Bartels–Lück, Freedman–Quinn), and the text does not say whether Π is good. The claim's conclusion is in tension with the good case, and the text does not discuss this.
entries.direction: disproves the homeomorphism-existence form of the Borel conjecture in dimension four, for one hyperbolic group; the self-map result also refutes the homotopy-realization form in dimension four
entries.object: Two closed aspherical topological four-manifolds M = M₀ and N = M_ℓ, and a self-homotopy equivalence f: M → M. M and N are built explicitly as gluings of copies of one compact topological four-manifold V with boundary S₂ (the double-cover filling, obtained from the smooth chamber double cover D₂ by replacing finitely many punctured S² × S² neighborhoods with four-balls), along a flag-no-square triangulation of S and a choice of linear functional ε on the label group A. Once these choices are fixed, the gluing recipe is explicit. The chamber D itself comes from the plumbing constructions of the companion manuscripts. The non-homeomorphism is proved by contradiction, and no invariant is exhibited. The self-map f is not written down: it is obtained by realizing an outer automorphism through the classification of maps between Eilenberg–MacLane spaces.
entries.conditional_on: Yes. (a) Two companion OpenAI manuscripts, neither read here: 'A marked tensor obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding' ([MT]) and 'A PD4 group without an aspherical manifold model' ([PD]), both OpenAI Math Release preprints dated September 24, 2026. The reflection input (Theorem 'Reflection and marked fillings') is stated by the authors as extracted from [PD, Sections 3–5] and uses [PD, Propositions 3.2, 4.6, 5.5]. The parity chamber data and the odd-cover non-filling use the plumbing blocks of [MT, Section 2.2], the chamber and cut constructions of [PD, Section 2], the marked algebraicity theorem [MT, Theorem 5.1] with [MT, Proposition 4.5 and Lemma 4.4], and the universal-development argument of [PD, Section 3]. (b) That Out(Π) is finite rests on a splitting theorem of Bestvina and Feighn (using Paulin's construction), cited and not proved in the text. (c) Standard results cited without proof: Davis's reflection-group framework, Chepoi's median-graph facts, Przytycki–Świątkowski's flag-no-square triangulations, Stallings's ends theorem, and the Švarc–Milnor lemma. The argument does not use Khan's results.
entries.doubts: (1) The two load-bearing inputs are imported, not proved here. Theorem 'Reflection and marked fillings' is presented as extracted from [PD, Sections 3–5]. The odd-cover non-filling (Proposition 'Odd covers do not fill') takes its edge-level input unchanged from [MT, Proposition 4.5 and Theorem 5.1], and the text says that what it verifies is only the assembly at vertices with both kinds of endpoint and the conversion of the four-slot laws. (2) The endpoint-assignment theorem is said to be argued 'in full', yet the same paragraph says its truncated differential forms and its two successive homologies come from [MT, Section 3]. (3) The introduction cites Khan's rigidity up to topological s-cobordism for closed aspherical four-manifolds with torsion-free word-hyperbolic fundamental group, and says the five-dimensional product theorem needs a good group. Theorem 'pair' concerns exactly torsion-free word-hyperbolic Π. The text never says whether Π is good and does not reconcile this with Khan's result. It says only that 'the dimension is essential to their topological conclusion'. (4) Finiteness of Out(Π) is obtained by citing the Bestvina–Feighn splitting theorem and applying the paper's own no-splitting lemma. The cited theorem is not proved in the text. (5) A search of all section files found no step flagged as sketched, conditional, or omitted, and no hedging beyond the imported inputs.
